story.headline: The dollar ended its best week in two months near a 19-month high. US producer prices kept a December Fed rate hike close to certain, and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said more rises are likely.

reads.policy: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly joined the officials saying more rate rises are likely, and a December Fed hike is close to certain. Europe, Britain and Japan are also expected to hike, but US rates are rising faster, so the gap keeps favouring the dollar.
reads.growth: Euro-area growth was confirmed at a decent pace for the summer quarter, but it did not lift the euro. The US economy still looks firmer than Australia, Canada or New Zealand, which keeps the dollar ahead of those currencies. US retail sales on Tuesday are the next check.
reads.inflation: US wholesale prices cooled a touch in October but still run far above what the Fed wants, so the pressure to hike stays. That keeps supporting the dollar. In Japan, a weak yen is pushing wholesale prices up fast.
reads.risk: Iran's claims of strikes in the Gulf were denied or unconfirmed, so markets stayed calm and the safe-haven franc and yen got no lift. The Aussie and kiwi, which track the market mood, ended the week near their lows.
reads.tot: Oil held near Thursday's jump, but the International Energy Agency says the market is back in surplus, which caps prices. Dearer oil helps the Canadian dollar and hurts energy buyers like Japan and the euro area. Gold stayed well below $4,000, taking some support from the Aussie.
reads.positioning: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, and this week's moves went their way. Their large bet on the yen keeps losing money as it weakens. The newest weekly report from US regulators had not been published by the close.
reads.fiscal: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%, and this was their biggest weekly rise in more than a year and a half. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but a growing deficit is a worry if buyers start asking for more.

fed.summary: The Federal Reserve held rates on October 28 with two officials voting to hike. Hot October inflation and firm talk from officials, most recently San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly, have made a December hike close to certain and lifted the dollar to its highest since April 2025.
fed.priced: December: hike near certain, a half-point move a small minority bet; more hikes expected next year.
fed.why: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's 2% goal, and wholesale prices barely cooled in October. Daly says inflation is spreading into services and rate rises are likely.
fed.watch: US retail sales on Tuesday and the Fed's October meeting minutes on Wednesday. The decision is December 9.

boc.summary: The Bank of Canada raised rates to 2.50% in October and said more may be needed. Two months of job losses have made a December hike doubtful.
boc.priced: December: hold is the base case; hike about one in three.
boc.why: Inflation is expected to stay above 3% through much of next year, but Canada's economy has stalled and is shedding jobs.
boc.watch: Oil prices and Gulf news, which move the loonie. The decision is December 9.

rbnz.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand held at 2.75% in October in a narrow vote. Rising unemployment has made a December hike less certain, and the kiwi sits near a 19-month low.
rbnz.priced: December: hike possible but not fully expected.
rbnz.why: Inflation pressures argue for a hike, but unemployment at its highest since 2015 argues for waiting.
rbnz.watch: The official election result on November 27. The decision is December 9.

ecb.summary: The European Central Bank held at 2.50% in October and a December hike is widely expected. Economists see it as the last for now, which leaves the euro trailing as US rates keep rising.
ecb.priced: December: hike widely expected, possibly the last for a while.
ecb.why: Euro-area inflation is about double the bank's goal, but growth is only modest and France's debt worries linger, so the bank has little room to keep hiking. President Christine Lagarde has given no new signal.
ecb.watch: Euro-area inflation figures and any word from Lagarde before the decision on December 17.

boj.summary: The Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, far below other major banks, and is expected to hike in December. The dollar briefly topped 160 yen again, a level where Japan has bought yen before.
boj.why: The weak yen is pushing Japanese wholesale prices up fast, up 7.1% from a year earlier in October. Some board members still warn against hiking too soon.
boj.watch: Whether Japan buys yen after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama's warning on currency swings. The decision is December 18.

rba.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised rates to 4.85% on November 3, the highest among the major banks, but hinted it may now pause. The Aussie fell to its lowest since January as that rate lead shrinks.
rba.priced: December: no firm pricing yet; the bank itself hinted at a pause.
rba.why: Inflation is above the bank's forecasts, but unemployment is at a five-year high and some economists think the hiking cycle is ending.
rba.watch: Australian jobs figures on Wednesday, November 18, at 6:30 PM CT. The decision is December 8.

boe.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% on November 5 and said more may follow. Markets still expect a second hike in December, though the pound has slipped as US rates rise faster.
boe.priced: December: a second hike more likely than not.
boe.why: High energy costs from the Middle East conflict keep UK inflation up, and solid growth means the bank need not fear its hike is hurting the economy.
boe.watch: UK inflation figures for October on Wednesday, November 18, at 1:00 AM CT. The decision is December 17.

snb.summary: The Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero and can sell francs if they get too strong. Low Swiss inflation means no hike is in sight.
snb.why: Swiss inflation is barely above zero, so the bank has no reason to raise rates and some room to cut if the franc climbs.
snb.watch: Swiss inflation figures and any flare-up that sends money into the franc. The decision is December 10.

USD.summary: The dollar sits in the middle of the board: rate and inflation support are partly offset by Democratic control of Congress. Rising US yields and firm Fed talk gave it its best week in two months.

notes.policy: A December Fed hike is close to certain, and officials keep talking about more rises next year.
notes.inflation: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's goal, which keeps pressure on it to raise rates.
notes.fiscal: With Democrats controlling Congress, President Trump's spending plans look harder to pass, which trims some support for the dollar.

EUR.summary: The euro sits near the bottom of the board: weak growth, dear energy and France's debt worries outweigh an expected December rate hike. Rising US yields pushed it to its lowest since April 2025.

notes.policy: A December European Central Bank hike is expected and may be the last for a while, while US rates keep rising, so the gap works against the euro.
notes.growth: Euro-area growth held at a modest pace in the summer, but business surveys have weakened and France's economy is struggling.
notes.inflation: Euro-area inflation is about double the bank's goal, which keeps a December hike on the table.
notes.tot: The euro area buys most of its energy abroad, so dear oil drains money out of the region, though the recent fall in prices eases that.
notes.positioning: Speculators hold one of their biggest bets against the euro in years, so good news could set off a sharp rebound as they close it.
notes.fiscal: France's high debt and shaky budget keep investors demanding extra pay to hold French bonds, which weighs on the euro.

GBP.summary: The pound sits near the top of the board after the Bank of England raised rates to 4.00% and signalled more may follow. Faster-rising US rates have still pushed it to its lowest in about three weeks.

notes.policy: The Bank of England hiked in November, and its governor said it is unlikely to be the last while the Middle East conflict lasts.
notes.growth: UK growth matched forecasts in the third quarter and business surveys are the strongest since February, even though shoppers have pulled back.
notes.inflation: UK inflation is at its highest in about a year, keeping pressure on the Bank of England.

JPY.summary: The yen sits low on the board because Japanese rates are far below others and Japan pays dearly for imported energy. A likely December rate hike and warnings from Japan's finance minister help only a little with the dollar near 160 yen.

notes.policy: The Bank of Japan's rate is far below others, and even a December hike leaves a wide gap with US rates.
notes.risk: The yen tends to gain when stock markets get scared, as they did in early November, and loses some of that pull when they calm.
notes.tot: Japan buys almost all its energy abroad, so oil holding near recent highs weighs on the yen.
notes.positioning: Speculators hold one of their biggest bets on the yen in years, and those bets lose money as the yen weakens, which could make them close fast.

CHF.summary: The franc sits in the middle of the board: its safe-haven pull is offset by inflation too low to need higher rates. The Swiss National Bank also says it can sell francs if they get too strong.

notes.inflation: Swiss inflation is low, so the central bank has no need to raise rates from zero.
notes.risk: The franc draws money when markets get nervous, but with stocks broadly holding up it has had little of that support lately.

AUD.summary: The Aussie scores well on the board thanks to the highest rates among the major central banks and firm commodity prices. It still fell to its lowest since January as US yields rose and gold slid.

notes.policy: Australia's interest rate is the highest among the major central banks, though the governor hinted at a pause and some economists see the hikes ending.
notes.growth: Australian unemployment is at a five-year high and home lending has slumped, though China's stronger buying helps exporters.
notes.inflation: Inflation is running above the Reserve Bank of Australia's forecasts, which kept it hiking.
notes.tot: Australia sells energy and metals abroad, but gold's slide below $4,000 takes some of that support away.
notes.positioning: Speculators are betting heavily against the Aussie, so better news could set off a sharp rebound as they close those bets.

CAD.summary: The Canadian dollar sits mid-board: the Bank of Canada's October hike and oil exports help, but job losses have cut bets on more hikes. Oil holding near recent highs has softened, not stopped, the drag from rising US rates.

notes.policy: The Bank of Canada raised rates in October and says more may be needed, though its meeting notes added no new signal and markets doubt a December move.
notes.growth: Canada lost jobs in September and October, and growth has stalled.
notes.inflation: Rising costs for Canadian producers point to more inflation ahead.
notes.tot: Oil has held up after attacks on Saudi energy sites, which gives the loonie a cushion.

NZD.summary: The kiwi sits low on the board because rising unemployment has cut bets on a December rate hike. Rising US yields have kept it close to its lowest in 19 months.

notes.growth: New Zealand's unemployment rose to its highest since 2015.
notes.tot: Firm prices for dairy, New Zealand's main export, and stronger Chinese buying support its earnings.
notes.positioning: Speculators are betting heavily against the kiwi, so better news could set off a sharp rebound as they close those bets.
